### a) Principle of Transmissibility
The Principle of Transmissibility states that the state of rest or motion of a rigid body is unaltered if a force acting on the body is replaced by another force of the same magnitude and direction acting along the same line of action (at any point along this line).

```text
[Force F] ---> (Point A) ===Line of Action=== (Point B) ---> [Force F]
```
- **Key Point:** It is only applicable to rigid bodies and helps in sliding forces along their line of action to simplify concurrent force system problems.

---

### b) Lami's Theorem
Lami's Theorem states that if three coplanar forces acting at a point are in equilibrium, then each force is proportional to the sine of the angle between the other two forces.

Mathematically, for forces $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$ with respective opposite angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$:
$$\frac{F_1}{\sin\alpha} = \frac{F_2}{\sin\beta} = \frac{F_3}{\sin\gamma}$$

```text
       F3
       ^  / F2
       | /
       |/___> F1
  Angles opposite to each force
```
proTip: Lami's theorem is exclusively applicable when there are exactly three concurrent coplanar forces in equilibrium.
